title: C++ foundations
blurb: The language as far as your notes go: initialisation, types and sizes, scope, linkage, namespaces and enums. No loops, no classes — none of these need them.
goal: Finish this and every idea in chapters 0 to 2 of your notes has been tested rather than only read.

title: First steps
blurb: Ten problems across the whole site, chosen so that each one needs only what the one before it taught. A reasonable first week.
goal: A tour of what is here, without hitting anything that needs background you have not got yet.

title: How memory really behaves
blurb: Alignment, cache lines, locality, virtual memory and the page-fault path — the thread that runs from sizeof all the way to a 4.5x slowdown from a loop order.
goal: Be able to explain why two loops doing identical arithmetic differ by eight times.

title: What the standard does not promise
blurb: Signed overflow, integer promotions, out-of-bounds reads, and the optimiser deleting a check you wrote. The most useful thing a C++ programmer can be frightened of.
goal: Stop reading "it worked at -O0" as evidence of anything.

title: Problems you write code for
blurb: Every code problem on the site, easiest first. Each compiles and runs for real, in C++ if you want it to.
goal: Six working programs, each one a thing worth having written once.
